solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Boxers giving jabs around beginning of round

indicators.note: around says the word for jabs is wrapped round the next letter

parts.note: giving jabs means delivering shots, as a boxer or a nurse might

indicators.note: beginning of picks out the opening letter of the word round

explanation.surface: A boxing match where the fighters land jabs at the start of a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' looks like the fighters but means the underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are loose men's underpants, so boxers are a kind of short trousers.

clue.text: …classy bar, it exists to trap sensualist

indicators.note: to trap says the answer is held within the run of words

explanation.surface: A smart bar existing to catch pleasure-seekers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite is a lover of luxury and pleasure, after the indulgent citizens of Sybaris.

clue.text: One improves view of work by artist reportedly

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: reportedly says the painter's name is taken as it sounds

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A painter's work praised as improving how a scene is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician tests eyes and supplies glasses, so helps people see better.

clue.text: In Paris very old hat, virtually wrong

parts.note: tres is French for very

indicators.note: virtually means almost all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: passe means old hat, out of date

explanation.surface: Paris fashion: a very old-fashioned hat, almost a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespass is a wrong or sin, as in the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Gleaming Gents finally with no bowl?

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word Gents

parts.note: a pot is a bowl-shaped vessel
less as a suffix means without, so with no gives it

explanation.surface: A men's lavatory left without its toilet bowl, perhaps surprisingly clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gents' is a British word for a men's public lavatory, which colours the 'bowl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spotless is perfectly clean, so it is gleaming.

clue.text: Upper-class degenerate, say, rolling in endless sin

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the trimmed sin
endless drops the last letter of the sin

parts.note: pride is one of the seven deadly sins
degenerate as an adjective means vile, depraved

indicators.note: rolling says the abbreviation for say turns over

parts.note: eg, for example, is said by say

explanation.surface: A decadent aristocrat wallowing in unending sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual crossword signal for 'for example'; 'rolling' turns only that abbreviation round, not the word for degenerate.
explanation.definitionFit: The privileged enjoy wealth and advantages, as the upper classes do.

clue.text: Backward, took test again tackling English problem

indicators.note: tackling means taking on, so the reversed word holds the next letter
backward says the resit word is read in reverse

parts.note: resat means sat an exam again

explanation.surface: A slow pupil resitting an exam and grappling with an English question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns RESAT into TASER, which then takes in E.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or tricky problem, short for brain-teaser.

clue.text: Produce the Italian volcano's first interior upset

indicators.note: first says the volcano comes before the Italian article
interior upset turns over only the middle pair of the volcano's letters

parts.note: Etna is the Sicilian volcano
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: The Italian volcano's interior first erupting upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior upset' turns over the middle letters of ETNA to give ENTA.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to bring about or involve as a consequence.

clue.text: Shelter for American Indian in daylight ends

indicators.note: in says the Cree go inside the ends
ends keeps only the outer letters of the daylight word

parts.note: the sun gives daylight
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A shelter for a Native American when the daylight ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is a barrier that shields or protects from view or wind.

clue.text: Superior person punting?

definitions.meaning: one who punts, i.e. places a bet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Punting' suggests boating on a river with a pole; here it is the slang sense of gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Better is a comparative of good meaning superior, and a bettor (also spelt this way) is one who wagers.

clue.text: Gesso covers top of Ionic column

indicators.note: covers says the plaster word goes round the next letter

parts.note: gesso is a plaster ground used by painters and sculptors

indicators.note: top of picks out the opening letter of the word Ionic

explanation.surface: A plaster coating applied over the head of a classical Ionic column.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column projecting from a wall.

clue.text: Means for majestic Queen to return

indicators.note: to return says the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: majestic in scale means epic
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A grand ceremony to bring the Queen back home.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe for success is the means of achieving it: a method or formula.

clue.text: Home of tree lodge overlooking river

parts.note: a fir is a conifer

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the river letter is left out

parts.note: to lodge somewhere is to reside there

explanation.surface: A tree lodge, a house up in the branches, looking down over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' paints a view; it means disregarding, dropping R from RESIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside stands for home and domestic life, as in a cosy hearth.

clue.text: Company shared in club entertainment creates shock

parts.note: a disco is a dance club

indicators.note: shared means the company letters are common to both words, so written only once

parts.note: a concert is a musical entertainment

explanation.surface: A firm's party at a club produces a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: DISCO ends and CONCERT begins with the same company letters; 'shared' says they appear once.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert is to unsettle or jolt someone.

clue.text: Reportedly dream French footballer comes to pass

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for dream is taken as it is heard

parts.note: a trance is a dreamlike state
Robert Pires is a French footballer, once of Arsenal

explanation.surface: News that a French footballer's dream has come true.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Pires was a French winger who starred for Arsenal in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpire is to happen or occur, the same idea as an event taking place.

clue.text: Idle horse, first to last in National

indicators.note: in says the altered horse goes inside the national word

parts.note: national as in state-owned, a state enterprise

indicators.note: first to last moves the opening letter of the horse word to its end

parts.note: a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A lazy horse finishing last in the Grand National.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' turns NAG into AGN. The Grand National is Britain's famous steeplechase horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stay inactive, the same as idling.

clue.text: Dead smell turning fish terrine case

indicators.note: turning says the smell letters turn round

parts.note: BO is body odour
sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: case takes the outer letters of terrine

explanation.surface: A dead fish in a terrine starting to smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete means no longer in use, so dead in a figurative sense.

clue.text: Ample sort embracing topless celebrity

indicators.note: embracing says the sort word wraps round the trimmed celebrity

parts.note: a genus is a sort or kind

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter of the celebrity word

parts.note: a hero is a celebrated person

explanation.surface: A buxom figure hugging a topless star.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous portions are plentiful, so lavish or large.

clue.text: OK Sauce evenly accompanying mushroom food

indicators.note: evenly takes the second and fourth letters of the word Sauce

parts.note: a cep is a porcini mushroom
table can mean the food served, as in a good table

explanation.surface: A restaurant critic approving a mushroom dish served with sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptable means satisfactory or all right.

clue.text: Shakespeare in speech is restrained

indicators.note: in speech says the word for Shakespeare is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Shakespeare is the Bard of Avon

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's verse, when spoken, sounds restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Barred means held back or prevented, as by bars.

clue.text: Lives and lives again under credit crunch

indicators.note: under says the lives words go beneath the credit letters

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
lives means is, exists
lives again is a second is

explanation.surface: Livelihoods suffering again and again in the credit crunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunch is a critical moment, an emergency.

clue.text: Greek city overturned Athens initially with ruses

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the joined pieces read upwards
initially picks the opening letter of Athens

parts.note: traps are ruses or tricks

explanation.surface: A Greek city overthrew Athens using tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: Athens is a red herring: Sparta, its old rival, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta is an ancient city-state of the Peloponnese.

clue.text: Drug left over stopping boundless hurt

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the turned word goes inside
boundless strips the outer letters, the bounds, from the word for hurt

parts.note: hurt as an adjective means pained

indicators.note: over says the word for left is turned round

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A painkiller left over, used to stop unlimited pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is the nautical sense, port; 'boundless' strips both outer letters from the word for hurt, leaving AINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is an alkaloid medicine from deadly nightshade, used to dilate pupils.

clue.text: Start to irrigate blood surrounding new cut

indicators.note: start to picks out the opening letter of irrigate
surrounding says the blood word goes around the next letter

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

explanation.surface: A medical instruction: irrigate the bloody area round a fresh cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a wound but is the social sense: to snub.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub or deliberately disregard them.

clue.text: Prayers producing sign by god without foundation

indicators.note: without foundation removes the base, here the opening letter of the god

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Prayers producing a sign from a god, though with no basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosaries are sequences of Catholic devotions counted on beads.

clue.text: Bowled over following look from pavilion

indicators.note: following says the cricket letters come after the look word

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowled out walks back after a glance from the pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket pavilion is where players watch from; here it is a garden summerhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small garden pavilion or summerhouse with a view.

clue.text: Back in toilet, sat sideways, showing revulsion

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone back in the lavatory, sitting awkwardly, pulling a face of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is dislike or aversion, though a noun rather than the adjectival phrase.

clue.text: Lush, oddly, always found inside bars…

indicators.note: found inside says the word for always goes within the odd letters
oddly takes the first and third letters of the word Lush

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A drunk always to be found in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' is slang for a drunkard, and 'bars' suggests pubs, but they are metal rods.
explanation.definitionFit: Levers are bars used to prise or lift things.
